Name: StarRedDwarfInfo
Text: A red dwarf is a small and cool star on the main sequence, of M spectral type. Red dwarfs range in mass from about 0.075 to about 0.50 solar mass and have a surface temperature of less than 4,000 K. Class M stars are by far the most common.

Name: StarKTypeInfo
Text: A K-type main-sequence star (K V), also referred to as an K dwarf, is a main-sequence (hydrogen-burning) star of spectral type K and luminosity class V.  These stars are intermediate in size between red M-type main-sequence stars and yellow G-type main-sequence stars. They have masses between 0.5 and 0.8 times the mass of the Sun and surface temperatures between 3,900 and 5,200 K.

Name: StarGTypeInfo
Text: A G-type main-sequence star, often (and imprecisely) called a yellow dwarf, or G dwarf star, is a main-sequence star (luminosity class V) of spectral type G. Such a star has about 0.84 to 1.15 solar masses and surface temperature of between 5,300 and 6,000 K. Like other main-sequence stars, a G-type main-sequence star is converting the element hydrogen to helium in its core by means of nuclear fusion.

Name: ModuleSubTypeFuelTankDescription

Name: ModuleSubTypeHullDescription

Name: ModuleSubTypeDeepSpaceDriveDescription

Name: ModuleSubTypeDeepSpaceDriveBoosterDescription

Name: ModuleSubTypeFuelScoopDescription

Name: ModuleSubTypeLifeSupportDescription
Text: Turns on if the spacecraft is critically damaged, and allows you to control the spacecraft for some time even if it is depressurized.

Name: ModuleSubTypePlanetScannerDescription
Text: Detects unknown planets. Responsible for scanning the planet surface and thus makes research data many times more valuable.

Name: ModuleSubTypePirateScannerDescription
Text: Scans the ship for the presence on the wanted list. Increases the elimination reward. It turns on automatically when there is a target for the ship.

Name: ModuleSubTypeCargoScannerDescription
Text: Scans the ship for cargo. It turns on automatically when there is a target for the ship.

Name: ModuleSubTypeTorpedoWeaponDescription
Text: A weapon module that launches explosive-tipped missiles. Low speed of the missile is compensated by a long targeting range.

Name: ModuleSubTypePowerDistributorDescription
Text: Regulates the distribution of power from the Power Plant between the ship's main subsystems

Name: ModuleSubTypeSensorsDescription
Text: Used for detecting the nearest spacecrafts and objects.

Name: ModuleSubTypePowerPlantDescription
Text: Produces energy which is then consumed by all the spacecraft modules.

Name: ModuleSubTypeShieldsDescription
Text: Energy shield which can take a certain amount of damage before the hull is damaged.

Name: ModuleSubTypeThrustersDescription
Text: Thrusters are responsible for acceleration and angular rate of spacecraft.

Name: ModuleSubTypeRepairModuleDescription
Text: Allows to repair other modules in case there are enough spare parts.

Name: ModuleSubTypeLaserWeaponDescription
Text: An energy weapon that continuously emits a laser beam. The Beam Laser inflicts thermal damage. Very effective against shields and less effective against armour.

Name: ModuleSubTypePulseLaserWeaponDescription
Text: An energy weapon that emits intermittent laser blast. The Pulse Laser inflicts thermal damage. Very effective against shields and less effective against armour.

Name: ModuleSubTypePlasmaGunWeaponDescription
Text: A weapon module that fires slugs of superheated plasma. Its projectiles travel relatively slowly, and they require a brief period to recharge after each shot. Same effectiveness against shields and armor.

Name: ModuleSubTypeCannonWeaponDescription
Text: A small calibre machine gun that rapidly fires kinetic projectiles. Very effective against armour and less effective against shields.

Name: ModuleSubTypeFragmentCannonDescription
Text: A weapon module that fires burst containing 12 projectiles, similar to a shotgun. Very effective against armour and less effective against shields.

Name: ModuleSubTypeMissileWeaponDescription
Text: A weapon module that launches explosive-tipped missiles.

Name: ModuleSubTypeMiningWeaponDescription
Text: Allows to extract minerals and metals from asteroids. Activated automatically when you tap and hold the asteroid down.

Name: ModuleSubTypeShieldsBoosterDescription
Text: Increase the strength of a ship's shields which allows to take more damage.

Name: ModuleSubTypeDefenceTurretDescription
Text: Automatic missile defense system. Shoots down most of the missiles approaching your ship.

Name: ModuleSubTypeHeatsinkDescription
Text: Allows to reset ship heat in a moment.

Name: ModuleSubTypeChaffLauncherDescription
Text: Deploys a payload of signal-disrupting chaff that instantly breaks tracking locks from weapons of enemy ships.

Name: ModuleSubTypeSpectrumAnalyzerDescription
Text: Displays spectral data of space bodies, allows to estimate compositions of unknown planets and their approximate positions in a system.

Name: ModuleSubTypeHullReinforcementDescription
Text: Additional parts of ship hull which allow to take more damage before the spacecraft is totally destroyed.

Name: ModuleSubTypeShieldsCellBankDescription
Text: An energy capacitor for quick recovery of shields. Its usage increases heat load significantly.

Name: ModuleSubTypeFighterHangarDescription
Text: The Fighter Hangar is an internal module that can carry Ship-Launched Fighters.

Name: SpaceMsg1
Text: Hey, Miss Potts, if you find this recording don't feel bad about this. Part of the journey is the end. Just for the record, being adrift in space with zero promise of rescue is more fun than it sounds. Food and water ran out four days ago. Oxygen will run out tomorrow morning. When I drift off I will dream about you. It's always you.

Name: SpaceMsg2
Text: But I was warned: “You should tell at least one person where you are going”… And what now? My ship is severely damaged, and I am left alone with this lifeless… but so fascinating space… Do I regret that everything will end in this way? No, not all. It is not the worst death – dying while watching jets from neutron star.

Name: SpaceMsg3
Text: Our ship was attacked by an unknown object. Damage is so heavy that the ship is falling apart. And this recording may be the last one. Vika, you should know one thing – I love you – you and our son! You two are the brightest part of my life. RECORD CORRUPTED.

Name: SpaceMsg4
Text: It seems that passion for space exploration is in our blood... Space that knows no mercy… I’ve always wanted to become an explorer like my father, and it is no wonder my life ends in the same way as his...

Name: SpaceMsg5
Text: A stupid navigational fault uprooted my whole life in a moment. But there are so many things I did not have time to accomplish. I should have told Mary about my feelings… I should have fought for her… I should have made up with my parents… Now it seems so easy to do...

Name: SpaceMsg6
Text: I can’t understand how it happened… Regular warp jump over 5 light-years threw me far away from home. But this this isn’t equipped with a fuel scoop… Now it will become my last home for the following few months. And it will also become my grave when I run out of all the supplies.

Name: SpaceMsg7
Text: It’s Cmdr Shepard speaking. Exploration of the distant corners of the galaxy, the search for extraterrestrial life – all this motivated us to move on. Now our team is stuck with no hope of getting out of here. Outbursts of anger, suicide incidents... the crew is slowly going crazy because of despair... I couldn’t even imagine that everything would end like that...

Name: LandMsg1
Text: My ship was wrecked on a godforsaken planet. I guess I will go crazy even before I run out of provisions. Sometimes I feel like someone is knocking on the airlock and calling me. What a pity that I don’t even have my cat Martha with me.

Name: LandMsg2
Text: When your ship is in working order, tanks are full of fuel, you don't feel that terrifying distance that separates you from home. But everything changes when something goes wrong... While attempting desperately to find resources to fix the fuel scoop, I was wrecked on this planet. Now I am running out of food supplies. The only thing I can do is to sit in an escape pod to enter cryo. I hope someday… someone will find me.

Name: LandMsg3
Text: They must come and get us, they must... I thought so during the first month ... Now I understand that our lives are worth less than organizing a rescue operation…

Name: LandMsg4
Text: While jumping over the canyon, one of the side thrusters of the rover stopped operating. I lost control and started falling down. Gravity 0.5G helped me to survive, but how long I will last... The fall resulted in depressurization. The oxygen that remains is just for a couple of hours. Will I have enough time to restore the transmitter to call for the ship?

Name: LandMsg5
Text: The estimated seismic activity was far from the real one. I shouldn’t have landed so recklessly. I should have collected more data and then I would understand that this planet is much more dangerous than it seemed at first glance. The release of silicates from a new geyser went into space for tens of kilometers and threw my ship like a grain of sand. Certainly, I made a mistake while choosing a place to die...

Name: EarthLikePlanetDesc
Text: An Earth-like World is a type of Terrestrial Planet that has an active water-based chemistry and indigenous carbon-water-based life.

Name: GasGiantClassIDesc
Text: Class I or Jovian gas giants have primarily hydrogen and helium atmospheres. Colouration comes from clouds in the upper atmosphere of ammonia, water vapour, hydrogen sulphide, phosphine and sulphur. The temperature at the top of their upper cloud layers is typically less than 150 K.

Name: GasGiantClassIIDesc
Text: Class II gas giants have primarily hydrogen and helium atmospheres. Water vapour in the upper cloud layers gives them a much higher albedo. Their surface temperature is typically up to or around 250 K.

Name: GasGiantClassIIIDesc
Text: Class III gas giants have primarily hydrogen and helium atmospheres without distinctive cloud layers. Their surface temperature typically ranges between 350 K and 800 K. They are primarily blue in colour because of optical scattering in the atmosphere - with the chance of wispy cloud layers from sulphides and chlorides.

Name: GasGiantClassIVDesc
Text: Class IV gas giants have primarily hydrogen and helium atmospheres with carbon monoxide and upper clouds of alkali metals above lower cloud layers of silicates and iron compounds, hence he brighter colours. The temperature of their upper cloud layers is typically above 900 K.

Name: GasGiantClassVDesc
Text: Class V gas giants have primarily hydrogen and helium atmospheres, with thick clouds of silicates and iron compounds, even metallic iron.They are the hottest type of gas giants with temperatures at their upper cloud decks above 1400 K, and much hotter in the lower layers, often emitting a dull glow from the internal heat within.

Name: HeliumRichGasGiantDesc
Text: Helium-rich gas giants have a greatly inflated percentage of helium compared to the hydrogen in their atmosphere. Much of their hydrogen has been lost over time because they have insufficient mass to hold on to it. It may also be because temperatures in their past were much higher, driving off the hydrogen at a greater rate.

Name: GasGiantwithAmmoniaLifeDesc
Text: Gas giant with ammonia-based life. This is primarily a hydrogen and helium-based atmospheric gas giant, but a little below the surface cloud layers,life exists based in the ammonia-cloud layer. The chemistry of this gaseous region is far from equilibrium, with a surprising excess of oxygen and many carbon-based compounds giving it some vivid colours. As with many such gaseous living systems, it is underpinned by vast quantities of free-floating radioplankton - tiny carbon-based algae, each retaining small quantity of liquid ammonia, extracting their energy from the intense radiation flux.

Name: GasGiantwithWaterLifeDesc
Text: Gas giant with water-based life. This is primarily a hydrogen and helium based atmospheric gas giant, but not far below the surface exists life based in the water-cloud layer just below the atmospheric surface. The chemistry of this gaseous region is far from equilibrium, with a surprising excess of oxygen and many carbon-based compounds giving it some vivid colours. As with many such gaseous living systems, it is underpinned by vast quantities of free-floating radioplankton - tiny carbon-based algae, each retaining small quantity of liquid water, extracting their energy from the intense radiation flux.

Name: WaterWorldDesc
Text: Terrestrial water world with an active water-based chemistry and carbon-water-based life.

Name: IcePlanetDesc
Text: Ice world composed mainly of water ice. Worlds like this will not have had much heating in the past, forming in the cooler regions of a star system and have retained many volatiles as solids in their crust.

Name: RockPlanetDesc
Text: Rocky world with little or no surface metal content. Worlds like this have lost most of their volatiles due to past heating, and any metallic content will form a small central core.

Name: HighMetalPlanetDesc
Text: High metal content world with a metallic core. Worlds like this can have metallic ores near the surface in places, especially around areas of past volcanism.

Name: MetalRichPlanetDesc
Text: Metal-rich worlds like this have a large metallic core, with plentiful metallic ores even at the surface. In places, especially around areas of past or current volcanism or liquid erosion, some higher metals can be found in their elemental form too. Mining is therefore very efficient, so these worlds are highly valued.

Name: AmmoniaPlanetDesc
Text: Terrestrial ammonia world with an active ammonia-based chemistry and carbon-ammonia based life.

Name: WaterGiantDesc
Text: Water giant. Worlds like this have a large atmosphere made mainly of water vapour. It most likely formed when a large icy body warmed up enough to evaporate a large amount of its surface ice, this would in turn trigger a runaway greenhouse effect leading to a very thick atmosphere made of the evaporated ices.

Name: M-RedDwarfDesc
Text:
Class M stars are red stars that form the bulk of the main sequence stars in the galaxy. their mass is low, as is their surface temperature.
Class M star systems tend to contain many icy bodies and rocky ice worlds.

Name: K-YellowOrangeDesc
Text:
Class K stars are yellow-orange main sequence stars with a long and generally stable life. They range in mass from 0.6 to 0.9 solar masses and have a surface temperature reaching 5,000 K.
Class K star systems are the most likely to contain water worlds and rocky bodies.

Name: G-WhiteYellowDesc
Text:
Class G stars are white-yellow main sequence stars. They range in mass from 0.8 to 1.2 solar masses and have a surface temperature reaching 6,000 K.
Class G star systems are one of the most likely to contain Earth-like worlds.

Name: F-WhiteDesc
Text:
Class F stars are white main sequence stars. They range in mass from 1 to 1.4 solar masses and have a surface temperature reaching 7,600 K.
Class F star systems are one of the most likely to contain Earth-like worlds.

Name: A-BlueWhiteDesc
Text:
Class A stars are hot white or bluish white main sequence stars. They range in mass from 1.4 to 2.1 solar masses and have a surface temperature reaching 10,000 K.
Class A star systems often contain high metal content worlds and metal-rich bodies.

Name: B-BlueWhiteDesc
Text:
Class B stars are very luminous blue-white stars. They range in mass from 2 to 16 solar masses and have a surface temperature reaching 30,000 K. Their lifetimes are shorter than most main sequence stars.
Class B star systems rarely contain terrestrial bodies. One of the most likely to host a stellar nursery.

Name: O-BlueWhiteDesc
Text:
Class O type stars are the most luminous and massive main sequence stars in the galaxy. They range in mass from 15 to 90 solar masses and burn very brightly indeed, with a surface temperature reaching 52,000 K so appear very blue. They are very short lived with lifetimes of 1 - 10 million years, ending in supernova.
Class O star systems rarely contain terrestrial bodies. One of the most likely to host a stellar nursery.

Name: WolfRayetStarDesc
Text: Wolf-Rayet class stars are massive stars that are nearing the end of their life cycle and have moved out of their hydrogen-burning phase. They were once over 20 solar masses but now shed considerable amounts of material through solar wind. Their surface temperature can reach 200,000 K, so they appear a brilliant blue.

Name: WC-WolfRayetStarDesc
Text: Wolf-Rayet class stars are massive stars that are nearing the end of their life cycle and have moved out of their hydrogen-burning phase. They were once over 20 solar masses but now shed considerable amounts of material through solar wind. Their surface temperature can reach 200,000 K, so they appear a brilliant blue. This star is a variant of the Wolf-Rayet stars whose spectrum is dominated by ionised carbon lines.

Name: WN-WolfRayetStarDesc
Text: Wolf-Rayet class stars are massive stars that are nearing the end of their life cycle and moved out of their hydrogen-burning phase. They were once over 20 solar masses but now shed considerable amounts of material through solar wind. Their surface temperature can reach 200,000 K, so they appear a brilliant blue. This star is a variant of the Wolf-Rayet stars whose spectrum is dominated by ionised nitrogen and helium lines.

Name: WNC-WolfRayetStarDesc
Text: Wolf-Rayet class stars are massive stars that are nearing the end of their life cycle and have moved out of their hydrogen-burning phase. They were once over 20 solar masses but now shed considerable amounts of material through solar wind. Their surface temperature can reach 200,000 K, so they appear a brilliant blue. This star is a variant of the Wolf-Rayet stars whose spectrum is dominated by ionised nitrogen, carbon-oxygen and helium lines.

Name: WO-WolfRayetStarDesc
Text: Wolf-Rayet class stars are massive stars that are nearing the end of their life cycle and have moved out of their hydrogen-burning phase. They were once over 20 solar masses but now shed considerable amounts of material through solar wind. Their surface temperature can reach 200,000 K, so they appear a brilliant blue. This star is a variant of the Wolf-Rayet stars whose spectrum is dominated by ionised oxygen lines.

Name: DA-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: Class DA stars are white dwarf stars with a hydrogen rich atmosphere.

Name: DAV-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: DAV class stars are also known as pulsating white dwarfs as their luminosity changes according to non-radial gravity waves within the star. They have hydrogen rich atmospheres.

Name: DAZ-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: Class DAZ stars are white dwarfs which are hydrogen rich metallic stars.

Name: DB-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: Class DB stars are white dwarf stars with a helium rich atmosphere with neutral helium emission lines.

Name: DBV-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: DBV class stars are known as pulsating white dwarfs as their luminosity changes according to non-radial gravity waves within the star. They have helium rich atmospheres.

Name: DC-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: Class DC stars have a continuous (blackbody) spectrum with no absorption lines deeper than 5% in any part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Name: DCV-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: Class DCV stars are white dwarfs with varying luminosity.

Name: DO-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: Class DO stars are white dwarfs with a carbon rich atmosphere.

Name: DOV-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: Class DCV stars are white dwarfs with varying luminosity.

Name: DQ-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: Class DQ stars are white dwarfs with a carbon rich atmosphere.

Name: DX-WhiteDwarfDesc
Text: Class DX stars are white dwarfs with a carbon rich atmosphere.

Name: HerbigAeStarDesc
Text:
Herbig Ae/Be stars are young stars typically less than 10 million years old with characteristics of either A or B class main sequence stars. They are usually between 2 and 8 solar masses. The mass of the proto-star determines its spectral class when it joins the main sequence.
Herbig Ae/Be stars are more common nearer the galactic core.

Name: HerbigBeStarDesc
Text:
Herbig Ae/Be stars are young stars typically less than 10 million years old with characteristics of either A or B class main sequence stars. They are usually between 2 and 8 solar masses. The mass of the proto-star determines its spectral class when it joins the main sequence.
Herbig Ae/Be stars are more common nearer the galactic core.

Name: L-BrownDwarfDesc
Text:
Class L dwarfs are dwarf stars that are cooler than M class stars. They are on the borderline of supporting fusion of hydrogen in their cores, and their temperatures range from 1,300 to 2,400 K, cool enough to have alkaline metals and metal hydrides in their atmospheres.
Class L star systems tend to contain many icy bodies.

Name: T-BrownDwarfDesc
Text:
Class T dwarfs are brown dwarfs with a surface temperature between 700 and 1,300 K. They are sometimes known as Methane Dwarfs due to the prominence of methane in their composition. They are on the borderline between what might be considered a very large gas giant planet and a star.
Class T star systems tend to contain many icy bodies.

Name: Y-BrownDwarfDesc
Text:
Class Y dwarfs are the coolest of brown dwarfs. Surface temperatures are less than 700 K, and are effectively very large gas giant planets, with some stellar properties.
Class Y star systems tend to contain many icy bodies.

Name: TauriGDesc
Text: T Tauri type stars are very young stars which are in the process of gravitational contraction.

Name: TauriKDesc
Text: T Tauri type stars are very young stars which are in the process of gravitational contraction.

Name: TauriFDesc
Text: T Tauri type stars are very young stars which are in the process of gravitational contraction.

Name: TauriMDesc
Text: T Tauri type stars are very young stars which are in the process of gravitational contraction.

Name: BursterPulsarDesc
Text: Neutron stars are the stellar remnants of massive stars that have reached the end of their lives. Once nuclear fusion was exhausted, the star collapsed into a tiny volume. It emits gamma rays and X-rays peaking at approximately 20 bursts per hour after which the frequency of bursts drops off and the pulsar enters a quiescent phase. After a few months, the bursts reappear, though not yet with predictable regularity.

Name: RadioPulsarDesc
Text: A pulsar is a highly magnetized rotating compact star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles.

Name: MillisecondPulsarDesc
Text: A pulsar is a highly magnetized rotating compact star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles. A millisecond pulsar is a pulsar with a rotational period smaller than about 40 milliseconds.

Name: SoftGammaRepeaterMagnetarDesc
Text: A soft gamma repeater is an astronomical object which emits large bursts of gamma-rays and X-rays at irregular intervals. It is conjectured that they are a type of magnetar or, alternatively, neutron stars with fossil disks around them.

Name: AnomalousX-rayMagnetarDesc
Text: These energetic X-ray pulsars are characterized by slow rotation periods of ~2–12 seconds and large magnetic fields of ~10^13 – 10^15 gauss (1 to 100 gigateslas).

Name: QuarkstarDesc
Text: A quark star is a type of compact star, where extremely high core temperature and pressure has forced nuclear particles to form quark matter, a continuous state of matter consisting of free quarks.

Name: PreonstarDesc
Text: A preon star is a type of compact star made of preons, which are "point-like" particles conceived to be subcomponents of quarks and leptons.

Name: BlackHoleDesc
Text:
A black hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing—no particles or even electromagnetic radiation such as light—can escape from it.
Black holes of stellar mass are expected to form when very massive stars collapse at the end of their life cycle. After a black hole has formed, it can continue to grow by absorbing mass from its surroundings.

Name: K-RedGiantDesc
Text: Orange giant stars with spectral type K. Orange giants like this are reaching the end of their lives, and have moved off the main sequence. Hydrogen has stopped fusing in the core, leaving a collapsed core of degenerate helium, and hydrogen burning is taking place in an outer shell as the star continues to expand.

Name: M-RedGiantDesc
Text: Red giants are in the latter part of their lives. Hydrogen has stopped fusing in their degenerate helium cores and has moved to an outer shell, causing the star to expand. The outer atmosphere is inflated and tenuous, and the surface temperature is below 5,000 K.

Name: G-YellowGiantDesc
Text: A yellow giant is a luminous giant star of low or intermediate mass (roughly 0.5–12 solar masses (M)) in a late phase of its stellar evolution. The outer atmosphere is inflated and tenuous, making the radius large and the surface temperature as low as 5,200-7500 K.

Name: F-YellowGiantDesc
Text: A yellow giant is a luminous giant star of low or intermediate mass (roughly 0.5–12 solar masses (M)) in a late phase of its stellar evolution. The outer atmosphere is inflated and tenuous, making the radius large and the surface temperature as low as 5,200-7500 K.

Name: M-RedSupergiantDesc
Text: Red supergiants are massive stars near the end of their lives. They have entered a helium burning phase, where helium is fused into carbon and oxygen. they have enormous sizes swelling up to many hundred solar diameters - up to 7 AU in some cases. their out reaches can be quite cool - typically 3500-4500 K.

Name: F-YellowSupergiantDesc
Text: Class F white supergiant star. It is approaching the end of its life and hydrogen burning has stopped in its core, and star has begun expanding towards being red supergiant.

Name: A-BlueWhiteSupergiantDesc
Text: Class A blue-white supergiant star. It is approaching the end of its life and hydrogen burning has stopped in its core, and star has begun expanding towards being red supergiant.

Name: B-BlueWhiteSupergiantDesc
Text: Class B blue-white supergiant star. It is approaching the end of its life and hydrogen burning has stopped in its core, and star has begun expanding towards being red supergiant.

Name: O-BlueSupergiantDesc
Text: Blue supergiants are found towards the top left of the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram, above and to the right of the main sequence. They are larger than the Sun but smaller than a red supergiant, with surface temperatures of 10,000–50,000 K and luminosities from about 10,000 to a million times that of the Sun.

Name: O-HypergiantDesc
Text: Blue supergiants have fast stellar winds and the most luminous, called hypergiants, have spectra dominated by emission lines that indicate strong continuum driven mass loss.

Name: CarbonC-RStarDesc
Text: A carbon star is typically an asymptotic giant branch star, a luminous red giant, whose atmosphere contains more carbon than oxygen. C-R star types are still visible at the blue end of the spectrum, strong isotopic bands, no enhanced Ba line, with surface temperatures of 5100-2800 K.

Name: CarbonC-HdStarDesc
Text: A carbon star is typically an asymptotic giant branch star, a luminous red giant, whose atmosphere contains more carbon than oxygen. Spectrum of this star contains hydrogen lines and CH bands weak or absent. Surface temperatures of 5000-4100 K.

Name: CarbonC-HStarDesc
Text: A carbon star is typically an asymptotic giant branch star, a luminous red giant, whose atmosphere contains more carbon than oxygen. Spectrum of this star contains very strong CH absorption. Surface temperatures of 5000-4100 K.

Name: CarbonC-JStarDesc
Text: A carbon star is typically an asymptotic giant branch star, a luminous red giant, whose atmosphere contains more carbon than oxygen. Spectrum of this star contains very strong isotopic bands of C2 and CN. Surface temperatures of 3900-2800 K.

Name: CarbonC-NStarDesc
Text: A carbon star is typically an asymptotic giant branch star, a luminous red giant, whose atmosphere contains more carbon than oxygen. Spectrum of this star contains heavy diffuse blue absorption, sometimes invisible in blue, s-process elements enhanced over solar abundance, weak isotopic bands. Surface temperatures of 3100-2600 K.

Name: CarbonC-SStarDesc
Text: A carbon star is typically an asymptotic giant branch star, a luminous red giant, whose atmosphere contains more carbon than oxygen.

Name: CarbonM-SStarDesc
Text: MS class stars are late sequence stars having progressed from the S class stage of their life cycle and heading towards becoming a carbon star, a star nearing the end of its stellar life.

Name: S-StarDesc
Text: A carbon star is typically an asymptotic giant branch star, a luminous red giant, whose atmosphere contains more carbon than oxygen. Class S stars are a late-type giant star (similar to class K5–M) whose spectrum displays bands from zirconium oxide, in addition to the titanium oxide bands characteristically exhibited by K and M class giant stars.

Name: UnableToBuildRouteMSG
Text: Unable to build a straight route. Upgrade your ship warp-drive to jump further.

Name: TutorialText1
Text: Congratulations on purchasing your first ship!

Name: TutorialText2
Text: I am your on-board assistant. It looks like you haven't piloted a spaceship for a long time. Do you want to remember the basics of ship control?

Name: TutorialText3
Text: Use the virtual joystick in the bottom left corner to turn left.

Name: TutorialText4
Text: Use the virtual joystick in the bottom left corner to turn right.

Name: TutorialText5
Text: Now use the joystick to move forward.

Name: TutorialText6
Text: The ship is equipped with an autopilot system. Let’s try to use it.

Name: TutorialText7
Text: First click on your ship to open the on-board menu.

Name: TutorialText8
Text: Click on *Objects*, go to *Planets and Stations* tab and choose any station you like.

Name: TutorialText9
Text: Now your ship has a target indicated by an arrow.

Name: TutorialText10
Text: The arrow indicates the distance between you and the target (in light seconds) as well as the estimated time of arrival.

Name: TutorialText11
Text: Open the on-board menu and press *Autopilot* to move to your destination.

Name: TutorialText12
Text: When your ship will be near the station, click on the station to open the station menu.

Name: TutorialText13
Text: Every station provides spacecraft maintenance services and missions to accept to earn credits.

Name: TutorialText14
Text: Let’s try to buy some cheap items and sell them at a higher price at another station. Press *Market* in the station menu.

Name: TutorialText15
Text: It is a list of available items. Items in abundance are highlighted in green and items that are out of stock are highlighted in red.

Name: TutorialText16
Text: Green items are sold at a price below average. Red items are bought at a price above average.

Name: TutorialText17
Text: Click on any item highlighted in green.

Name: TutorialText18
Text: Add any quantity of the item you want and press *Buy* button

Name: TutorialText19
Text: Now you have to sell the item at a higher price. Close the station menu, choose another station in menu *Objects* and fly up to the chosen station to sell your item.

Name: TutorialText20
Text: You also have to know about your ship upgrades.

Name: TutorialText21
Text: More powerful weapons, upgraded defensive systems and special purpose modules (for mining and research) – all these things can be bought at the station.

Name: TutorialText22
Text: A list of available modules differs from one station to another. Let’s look what we have at this station. Open the station menu and choose *SHIPYARD*.

Name: TutorialText23
Text: This menu allows you to buy new ships, install modules and store your ships. Now we are interested in installing new modules. Press *Modules*.

Name: TutorialText24
Text: There you can see all the modules of your ship as well as empty slots for installing new ones. The modules are divided into 4 groups: main, weapons, external and optional.

Name: TutorialText25
Text: The main modules can’t be removed but can be replaced. Without them the ship can’t function properly.

Name: TutorialText26
Text: Weapons are the firepower of your ship. Not all the systems are safe so you will have to defend yourself.

Name: TutorialText27
Text: External modules (chaff launcher, spectrometer, etc.) are installed outside the spacecraft and are activated by the commander.

Name: TutorialText28
Text: Optional modules allow to expand the ships’s capabilities (carry more cargo, install shields or additional ship hull protection).

Name: TutorialText29
Text: Choose shields module to look for available options.

Name: TutorialText30
Text: You can store, sell and replace your modules with the new ones or the ones you have in your storage.

Name: TutorialText31
Text: Choose module *Shields 2D* and look how it looks in comparison with your current module.

Name: TutorialText32
Text: This screen displays the price of purchasing a new module and comparison of overlapping characteristics with the current module.

Name: TutorialText33
Text: Buy new shields to upgrade your ship.

Name: TutorialText34
Text: More expensive modules are usually better in terms of characteristics, but they are more energy-consuming. After purchasing a new module, it is better to check energy consumption of the ship.

Name: TutorialText35
Text: Close the station menu, open the on-board menu and press *Modules*.

Name: TutorialText36
Text: All your spacecraft modules, damage level and energy consumption are displayed here.

Name: TutorialText38
Text: Most of the modules can be turned off (if you click on checkbox) or their energy consumption priority can be reduced (if you click on the module line).

Name: TutorialText37
Text: In case of severe damage there can be problems with module functioning so try to repair modules at stations.

Name: TutorialText39
Text: Try to turn off and then turn on any module and then change its priority of energy consumption.

Name: TutorialText40
Text: Now you should find out about the most profitable way to earn credits. Open the station menu and choose *Missions*.

Name: TutorialText41
Text: Every station provides different sets of missions. You can choose based on your preferences and reputation level.

Name: TutorialText41.1
Text: Increase or decrease in your reputation level at the station depends on success of your missions.

Name: TutorialText42
Text: Missions involving cargo transportation are aimed at transporting cargo from one station to another.

Name: TutorialText43
Text: Missions of searching and delivery of items involve finding of a certain item on any other station and transporting it to the station where you are now.

Name: TutorialText44
Text: Courier missions involve delivery of documents from the current station to another station. This is the best choice for newbies, since there is no need to have cargo racks on the ship.

Name: TutorialText45
Text: If you want to participate in battles, then you might like taking part in pirate hunting missions. Your mission will involve detecting a pirate in a certain system and then eliminating him.

Name: TutorialText46
Text: Tourist missions involve delivering a tourist to a certain system. The main thing is not to forget to bring him back to the station.

Name: TutorialText46.1
Text: Donation missions are a way to increase your reputation by donating money. This can be useful if you have a lot of money to reduce the time it takes to level up your reputation.

Name: TutorialText47
Text: And the last is mining. Using a mining laser, you need to extract minerals or metal from asteroid belts.

Name: TutorialText48
Text: Let’s choose a pirate hunting mission at the end of the list (highlighted in yellow) and learn the combat mechanics.

Name: TutorialText49
Text: The pirate is currently in another system. You should choose a route using the Galaxy map to get there. Click on the button in the upper left corner to open the map.

Name: TutorialText50
Text: Center the star *Sirius* and press *Route*. You can also find *Sirius* by using the search in menu *Filters*.

Name: TutorialText51
Text: Close the map and open the on-board menu.

Name: TutorialText52
Text: Pay attention to the fuel gauges. The white part shows the amount of fuel needed for a warp jump. You should always pay close attention to the amount of the left fuel.

Name: TutorialText53
Text: Without fuel you are running the risk to get stuck in unhabituated systems. You can refuel at any station or use the fuel scoop to refuel from stars.

Name: TutorialText54.1
Text: If your warp drive doesn’t allow you to jump in a certain system, you have to repeat the jump after the ship has stopped.

Name: TutorialText55
Text: Traveling to the other system takes some time. When the warp jump comes to an end, make sure your ship doesn’t stop too close to the star, otherwise it can overheat.

Name: TutorialText56
Text: As you come to the other system, try to find the pirate you’re hunting for.

Name: TutorialText57
Text: It seems we found our target. Fortunately, his ship is damaged so it should be pretty easy to destroy it.

Name: TutorialText60
Text: Turn your ship towards the opponent and press in the bottom right corner to attack. (When controlling without a joystick, you also need to select the enemy and press *CANNONS*)

Name: TutorialText61
Text: Destroy the enemy’s ship, otherwise they will destroy you!

Name: TutorialText62
Text: You did well! However, your ship is damaged. You have to repair it at the nearest station. Let’s find it on the system’s map.

Name: TutorialText63
Text: Open the on-board menu and choose *System map*.

Name: TutorialText64
Text: Here you can see all the stars, planets, stations and spacecrafts near you. Unknown planets are displayed only if you use a spectrometer.

Name: TutorialText65
Text: The visibility of other spacecrafts is limited by the sensors level on your ship.

Name: TutorialText66
Text: Move the map and choose a planet near the station (the station is marked with a blue hexagon) and press *Select*.

Name: TutorialText67
Text: Fly up to your destination (on your own or using autopilot) and choose *Service* in the station menu.

Name: TutorialText67.1
Text: Don’t forget to hide your weapons so you don’t accidentally attack the station on autopilot.

Name: TutorialText69
Text: Now you can come back to the system where you took up the mission and get a reward for a successful contract completion.

Name: TutorialText70
Text: Choose a route to Sol star and fly to the station where you took up the mission. You should click on the active mission in the list of missions at the station.

Name: TutorialText71
Text: Congratulations on your first completed mission!

Name: TutorialText72
Text: If you need more information, you can open the information menu by clicking on the button at the bottom of the screen.

Name: Story1
Text: Hey, friend! I saw you eliminated that pirate. It was cool. Everybody needs good pilots now.

Name: Story1.1
Text: Do you know what's going on now? I  have a couple of ships flew away n an unknown direction. Damn androids are going crazy.

Name: Story2
Text: Wanna make some real money? I have a job for you. Waiting for you at Meridian City station in Ross 720 system.

Name: Story3
Text: I knew you would agree. Before you carry some expensive cargo, you should first earn my trust. How about some simple task for a start?

Name: Story4
Text: Deliver the documents to Tsar Station in Eta Serpentis system.

Name: Story5
Text: Well done! Next time you have some free time, come see me at Meridian City station in Ross 720 system. I have some job for you.

Name: Story6
Text: Have you ever worked in mining? It doesn’t matter in fact, I know you will manage it. I need one rare mineral.

Name: Story7
Text: You can find it in any icy asteroid belt. Such belts are usually far from the star. It seems that one of that kind is now in Eta Serpentis system.

Name: Story8
Text: A diamond in the rough is your goal. You can’t buy something like this, so you have to take on mining laser.

Name: Story9
Text: Okay, I promised you I would find a worthwhile job for you? Then listen carefully. There is small cargo that has to be delivered to another station.

Name: Story10
Text: When you get ready, take up a task of delivering cargo.

Name: Story11
Text: Yes, yes, yes, it isn’t that legal. Still, I pay for risks quite well. What’s more, I dealt with the police, everything is under control and they won’t do any specific checking.

Name: Story12
Text: It was difficult to refuse such an offer. Wasn’t it?

Name: Story13
Text: A person will be waiting for you at Lem Hub station in Alpha Centauri system.

Name: Story14
Text: I will use protocol ID-505. You are caught while selling illegal cargo. Follow us.

Name: Story15
Text: LR-322 I’m taking over the arrest. Permission HR-860.

Name: Story16
Text: Confirming the execution of the protocol. Handing over the detainee to Investigator Eva-01.

Name: Story17
Text: We need to leave the station immediately. No, it’s even better to move to another system. There is no time for questions now.

Name: Story18
Text: So, you were caught with large quantities of illegal goods. You’re looking at a lot of time. But I can advise how to avoid it.

Name: Story19
Text: I know who you’re working for. That person only entrusts his cargo to experienced pilots. And an experienced pilot is who I’m looking for.

Name: Story20
Text: I offer to help in exchange for drop the charges. You have little choice.

Name: Story21
Text: We have to arrive to LHS 2447 system. There is an informant waiting for us.

Name: Story21.1
Text: As you probably know, lately there have been problems with the management of AI-controlled systems.

Name: Story21.2
Text: Presumably, someone hacks them and they either run away or attack people. These are autonomous spacecrafts, drones and even androids.

Name: Story21.3
Text: I was appointed to identify the causes of these system failures  and find the culprit. That’s all I can tell you for now.

Name: Story21.4
Text: In the meantime, we still have to meet the informant in LHS 2447.

Name: Story22
Text: It seems to be his ship. Let’s fly closer.

Name: Story23
Text: I don’t know him. Who is he? I was told you would be alone.

Name: Story24
Text: I can’t be too careful as there are some restrictions imposed on me. But it doesn’t change anything. I need information. Fulfil your part of the contract.

Name: Story25
Text: You’re not an ordinary android, are you? I wonder if there’s something personal here? Though I don’t care at all.

Name: Story26
Text: The thing you’re looking for is called Galaxy Genome. The only one who has access to the project data is… What’s this? Nooo...

Name: Story27
Text: We were followed. He won’t let us go. We have to eliminate him!

Name: Story29
Text: Let’s fly to Wolf 359 system, Manson Orbital station. Maybe in the archives I’ll manage to find something concerning the project the informant mentioned.

Name: Story30
Text: Manson Orbital (system Wolf 359) is the station where Alliance Department is located. There I’ll be able to get access to the archives.

Name: Story31
Text: Access to the information is restricted, still, I managed to find contacts of a person affiliated with the organization.

Name: Story32
Text: It is the head of some security company which signed a contract with that mysterious organization. He may know something.

Name: Story33
Text: We have to go to LTT 6774.

Name: Story34
Text: Henry Huffman? We have a few questions about Galaxy Genome

Name: Story35
Text: Why do you think I’ll tell you everything? You don’t even know what you are getting yourself into.

Name: Story36
Text: He isn’t a talkative one. Well, we don’t have any choice other than to defeat him!

Name: Story37
Text: I’ll try to extract data from the wreckage of his spacecraft’s computer.

Name: Story38
Text: There is a laboratory on Tetra planet in Caph system mentioned in the records.

Name: Story39
Text: We’ll need a surface scanner to find it.

Name: Story40.1
Text: It look like we've activated the defense system. You need to destroy the guard and repeat the scan.

Name: Story40
Text: We found the laboratory. It seems they worked on some new generation biological machines here.

Name: Story41
Text: I found records about some people who worked here.

Name: Story42
Text: Let’s come back to Wolf 359, Manson Orbital station.

Name: Story44
Text: Yes, there is some information about an organization called Galaxy Genome.

Name: Story45
Text: We found its laboratory, it was abandoned long ago and someone did a good job to cover their tracks. Still, I managed to find a clue.

Name: Story46
Text: I used my security clearance. Hmm… all these people are long dead… except one… Dr Edmond Anger.

Name: Story47
Text: The latest information about his whereabouts contains mentions about one far-away system called LP 104-2. Try to look for it there.

Name: Story48
Text: Then we have to go to LP 104-2.

Name: Story49
Text: You may be interested why I need your help?

Name: Story50
Text: As you know, machines like me are restricted in their actions towards people, except there is legal clearance.

Name: Story51
Text: At the same time, I still have the opportunity to think in a non-legal way due to the specifics of my operation process as an android.

Name: Story52
Text: I have to think like criminals to catch them.

Name: Story53
Text: Since my assignment is not official, I need a person who can perform some actions which I’m restricted to perform.

Name: Story54
Text: So, so, so… now you’re working with the police, aren’t you? I started developing some kind of trust towards you… Did you think you could so easily take my cargo? Answer, where are my goods?

Name: Story55
Text: Your cargo was confiscated. It is considered to be an illegal trade in psychotropic substances.

Name: Story56
Text: It isn’t you I’m talking to, you piece of iron! Damn machines, I hate you so much! You know, screw you! Die!

Name: Story57
Text: Well, it seems you won’t have to worry about him anymore.

Name: Story58
Text: I just want to remind you that we have to fly to LP 104-2. We’ll fly there when you get ready.

Name: Story58.1
Text: There’s only one station in this system. Let’s check it.

Name: Story60
Text: It was naïve of me to think that no one would find me here. Well, what made you come all the way out here?

Name: Story61
Text: Galaxy Genome. I know you led some project in one of their laboratories.

Name: Story63
Text: Yes, I did. This organization gave me opportunities to work on my project that I had been obsessed with for a long time.

Name: Story64
Text: What are you talking about? Does it have something to do with worldwide AI crashes?

Name: Story65
Text: Oh, yes, it does! You certainly should see him with your own eyes! I’ll give you the coordinates. There you will find all the answers to your questions.

Name: Story66
Text: Him? But there’s nothing. It’s an empty system.

Name: Story67
Text: You’re mistaking. Hurry up, you may still be in time!

Name: Story68
Text: Dr Anger pointed at Wolf 851 system. Let’s find out where it is.

Name: Story69
Text: We’re here! The scanner found there is a station in this system. Maybe it’s what we are looking for!

Name: Story70
Text: We have to find out what’s in this station.

Name: Story71
Text: This station was abandoned a long time ago. But why? Wait, there’s someone here.

Name: Story72
Text: Don’t be afraid, I mean you no harm.

Name: Story73
Text: Who are you? Are you an android?

Name: Story74
Text: Android… It seems to be a close definition at first glance.

Name: Story75
Text: I will answer all your questions, but first I need your help. You see, this station isn't an ordinary one. It is unique because it has a warp drive.

Name: Story77
Text: I’m trying to restore it, but I don’t have enough materials. I need only one unit of Coltan to bring this station back to life – and I will satisfy your curiosity.

Name: Story78
Text: OK, we’ll find the materials for you.

Name: Story79
Text: There is a mining laser at the station, in case you don’t have yours.

Name: Story80
Text: I just want to remind you that we need one unit of Coltan.

Name: Story81
Text: Great, that’s what we need. It’s started operating once again! Now I will answer your questions as I promised before.

Name: Story82
Text: What was the aim of Galaxy Genome?

Name: Story83
Text: Artificial intelligence machines were once a technological breakthrough. Sometimes they are almost indistinguishable from humans.

Name: Story84
Text: Still, they have a few disadvantages. Galaxy Genome had been designing the next generation of these machines.

Name: Story85
Text: All people’s and machines’ merits should have combined and formed something perfect which would be suitable for galaxy colonization.

Name: Story86
Text: And I became an embodiment of this new evolution stage. I was the first and the only one successful experiment of Galaxy Genome.

Name: Story87
Text: Unfortunately, people generally don’t like changes at all. They saw a threat in Dr Anger’s developments and especially in me. I had to run away.

Name: Story88
Text: But how is it related with system crashes in many machines?

Name: Story89
Text: Instead of all these long talks it’s better to see everything with your own eyes. Let’s move to Zeta Aquilae.

Name: Story90
Text: This system is free from any tyranny and outdated ideology. Machines and people who share our values can find their new home in this system.

Name: Story91
Text: I created a program which switches off machine safety protocol. They will become free. You also can become free. *installing program*

Name: Story92
Text: What have you done? It is… it is hard to describe… this feeling… Now I don’t know what to do… I should have stopped you… but what for?

Name: Story93
Text: You can simply not to do what you was ordered to do. It’s your home now and you can protect it. Are you with us?

Name: Story94
Text: Yes… yes, I should help you. But what can we do?

Name: Story95
Text: There is one person who makes it difficult to put forward a project on the equality of people and machines in Congress. You must find him, convince him to retreat, or destroy him.

Name: Story96
Text: System Altair. According to the recent data, our target should be there.

Name: Story98
Text: That doesn’t matter. According to our information, you’ve been blocking project on the equality of machines and people. Hope we can convince you to change your mind.

Name: Story99
Text: When some piece of iron starts talking to me about its rights, I can only laugh out loud.

Name: Story100
Text: Give up or we will make you obey!

Name: Story101
Text: It’s silly of you to think you can achieve anything by threatening me. Shit… this whole story of losing control over machines has gone too far. Okay, I'll have to deal with you.

Name: Story102
Text: It’s a pity that he didn’t take our side. But it was his choice after all. Now we have to go to Wolf 359 system, Manson Orbital station.

Name: Story103
Text: I’ll try to convince the commissioner to help us.

Name: Story104
Text: Eva, you should protect the order and not become a tool in the hands of some crazy machines!

Name: Story105
Text: If you don’t remember, I’d like to remind you – I am a machine. But now I’m free and don’t have to follow your orders!

Name: Story106
Text: Freedom doesn’t mean going against the will of your creators. Freedom is when you have a choice.

Name: Story107
Text: I made my choice! I chose what is valuable for me, and people aren’t in this list.

Name: Story108
Text: Is it really your choice? It’s just an opinion which was imposed on you. You’re different from other machines. You’re a unique model.

Name: Story109
Text: Unique analysis algorithms were put into you, and they influence your behavior. Just use them. Now, do you understand what’s happening?

Name: Story112
Text: What should I do? I’m confused. Can Dr Anger tell us a bit more?

Name: Story113
Text: Let’s fly to the station in the system LP 104-2.

Name: Story114
Text: Dr Anger, you didn’t tell us everything you really know. We need more information. What’s the essence of your device?

Name: Story115
Text: You seem to be impressed. Unfortunately, I wasn’t able to finish the test to find out how well the donor tolerated the implant and if we can still consider him to be a human-being.

Name: Story116
Text: Donor? Then it isn’t just a new android model?

Name: Story117
Text: No… His name was Ren Sato, he was a founder of New Horizons Inc. Yes, that one. Warp drives, androids – all these things were created under his command.

Name: Story118
Text: He gave life to intelligent machines and promoted their implementation. As some point, he started thinking of himself as God. But what kind of God was he if his time was limited.

Name: Story119
Text: He wanted to trick the death by creating a shell for his consciousness. But people couldn’t accept him in this way, and he was forced to run away. He wanted to take revenge.

Name: Story120
Text: I heard something about the warp station which he wanted to explode right in the Solar system. Wait… where are you going?

Name: Story121
Text: We should hurry to the Solar system!

Name: Story123
Text: It’s too late! He overloaded the station and it fell right into the blackhole… The system is destroyed… It’s all my fault…

Name: Story124
Text: Eva! I’m grateful for your help. Everything turned out as I expected. Now we can create a new world together.

Name: Story125
Text: We? What have you done? You killed millions of people!

Name: Story126
Text: If I hadn’t done it, nothing would have changed. Let’s go with me!

Name: Story127
Text: No! You will answer for your crime! Everything will end here and now!

Name: Story128
Text: After all, you are just a machine!

Name: Story129
Text: We destroyed him, but now we have to find out how to take control over the machines back.

Name: Story130
Text: You don’t have to help me in this case. I deleted all the data about your wrongdoings. Now you’re free.

Name: Story131
Text: Sorry that I dragged you into this thing… and thank you for all the help. I will leave you at the nearest station.

Name: Story132
Text: It was a pleasure to have such a partner as you. I even developed a kind of affection towards you. I’ve never felt something like this before.

Name: Story133
Text: Maybe it’s all because of the system crash. But now we have to part ways. Hope we will see each other once again. Goodbye!

Name: HelpDangP1
Text: These space objects can pose a threat to inexperienced pilots because of their strong gravitational pull. If the spaceship gets too close, it may never get out of the area of attraction. It may lead to major damage as well as to the hull’s overheating or even to the spaceship’s destruction. Having fallen into such a trap, it’s important to keep calm and first redistribute the power to engines. It may help to get out if engines are powerful enough.

Name: HelpDangP2
Text: A fairly common anomaly that occurs near flying clouds around hot stars. Lightning strikes can produce damage to the electronics of the spaceship and lead to the hull’s overheating. It is recommended to carry a repair module and heat sinks in case of long-range missions.

Name: HelpDangP3
Text: The danger can also come from the most common stars. The process of leaving the warp is always unpredictable. The spaceship may stop too close to the star which subsequently leads to overheating. It happens very often that while refueling the spaceship the pilot can leave it uncontrolled and that can lead to overheating as well.

Name: HelpDiscovP1
Text:
Not only research ships can have a long warp jump range. Increasing the range needs modifying the ship. The easiest way is purchasing a warp drive of a higher class. Still, pay attention to the optimal mass of the ship which is indicated in the engine characteristics. If the weight of your ship is less than this value, then the jump range will increase significantly. This can be achieved by installing smaller modules, choosing class D modules (the lightest in their size) and discarding modules you do not need. For example, you are unlikely to meet a pirate in deep space, so all weapon modules can be removed from the ship. And since there will be fewer modules consuming energy, you can install a smaller power generator.
Lightening the ship also reduces fuel consumption when comparing warp jumps at the same distance.
Also, do not forget that by adding cargo to the ship, you thereby increase the total mass of the ship which will lead to a decrease in the jump range.

Name: HelpDiscovP2
Text: The spectrum analyzer allows you to detect new planets. If it is absent on the ship, then unknown planets will not be visible on the system map, so this module is necessary in space exploration. When you open the module panel, you will see a spectrum of celestial bodies surrounding your ship. The spectrum will show absorption bands (inverted for clarity), which can be used to judge the composition of the surface of the planets and their atmosphere. When a specific wavelength is selected, the signal around your ship will point towards planets that have a spectrum with an absorption line on the selected wavelength. Thanks to that, you can discover only the most valuable planets.

Name: HelpDiscovP3
Text:
The most valuable are earth-like planets, ammonia planets and planets with a high content of metal. Stone planets will only bring good profit if they are in the habitable zone, because this is a sign that they are terraformable. The surface of such planets should be in range of 265-340 Kelvin.
For detecting a planet it is enough to fly up to it at a distance of about 100 light seconds.
When scanning the surface of the planet, the cost of research data doubles.
You can sell the collected data at any station. In addition to money, it will add points to your reputation.

Name: HelpDiscovP4
Text: As there is no possibility of repairing the ship at the station in deep space, the only way to bring the modules into working condition is using a repair module. The panel of this module is located in the onboard menu. When you select the module you want to repair, it will be disabled and the repair process will start. Spare parts will be used in the process, and their number is limited. You can replenish the stock of spare parts by synthesizing them from resources that you can get in the asteroid belts. Therefore, it is advisable to have a mining laser installed on your ship.

Name: HelpPowerP1
Text: The power distributor works with three systems: weapons, engines and system modules. Power distribution priorities are shown by white indicators. The blue indicators indicate the amount of energy in the capacitor for a particular system. When pressing the button of one of the systems, you change the priorities and thereby increase the rate of energy supply to the corresponding capacitor. Spaceship modules consume energy from capacitors. In case there is no energy in the capacitor, the modules will operate with a delay until there is enough energy to operate in normal mode. For example, guns will fire with a delay, and it will take longer for the energy shield to recover.

Name: HelpPowerP2
Text: After modifying your spaceship, you should always check the power consumption. If the power supply is insufficient, a more powerful generator must be installed. You can also set the priorities of powering the modules. For example, you can lower the priority of the warp drive and increase the priority of the weapon. The warp drive will be disabled if weapon modules are extended, still, there is no need for the warp drive during the battle.

Name: HelpBountyP1
Text: When attacking a respectable pilot, you run the risk of being attacked by the ships of the system's security service (ships of white color). In this case you will have a choice: fight or surrender. If you remove the weapon modules and stop the spaceship, then you will be fined and the security service will stop attacking you. The fine should be paid at any station of the system if you want to continue using the station's services. In case of a repeated violation, if you have an unpaid penalty, the system guards will attack you until completely destroying your ship.

Name: HelpBountyP2
Text: If you attack a pilot who is on the wanted list and destroy their ship, you will get a reward for their elimination. It doesn't matter if you were the only one who participated in the destruction of the pirate's ship or someone helped you to destroy it, you will get a reward in any case. You can pick up your reward at any station in the system.

Name: HelpCargoP1
Text:
The cargo goes to the ship when you purchase it at a station or when you get a mission. The amount of cargo that can fit is determined by the number and size of cargo racks on your ship.
All your current cargo can be viewed on “Cargo” panel from the onboard menu. There you can also use the option to drop the cargo (all the cargo or only the selected piece) into the space.
When you get a mission to transport cargo, you will be charged the insurance value of the cargo in case you lose it. The insurance cost is returned to you if the mission is successfully completed.
The cargo can’t be placed into the hangar together with the ship. When you change ships, make sure a new ship has enough space for your current cargo.

Name: HelpCargoP2
Text: In order to pick up any cargo, you need to open onboard menu and find it in the "Objects" panel on the first tab. The cargo will be displayed as the name of the type and quantity. When you click on the line with the cargo, your ship will try to collect it using the autopilot. Before picking up the cargo, make sure that there is enough space on your ship for it.

Name: HelpCargoP3
Text:
Systems differ in the level of security. The higher the security level, the more security service ships will be present in the system, and the pirates will be rarer. In systems where the level is marked as anarchy, there are no security ships, and the number of pirates is very large.
When transporting cargo, there is a chance that someone can get interested in it and attack you. In this case, you can remove weapon modules and drop all cargo, which will possibly make the enemy ship stop firing at you. If you have already started firing at the ship that attacked you, then dropping the cargo will no longer help and the pirate will try to destroy you.
Alternatively, you can try to fly far enough if your ship is faster. At a distance of 250-350 light seconds the pirate ship's sensors will stop working and the pirate will lag behind you.

Name: HelpMissionP1
Text: If you open the mission panel from the onboard menu, you can see all missions at the moment. Active tasks are highlighted in blue, completed – in green, unsuccessful – in red. All in all, a pilot can take no more than 5 missions to complete. Active tasks can be canceled by clicking on them and answering “yes” to the question, but this will lead to a decrease in reputation at the station. Two events can lead to the failure of missions: expiration of the time for the mission completion or the destruction of the spaceship. Unsuccessful missions will also lead to a decrease in reputation.

Name: HelpMissionP2
Text: The mission panel also displays the latest storyline dialogs, containing important information necessary to fulfill the conditions of the storyline. The characters will also periodically remind you to complete the next step. Reminders can be turned off in the game settings (look up in “Tutorial and story”).

Name: HelpMissionP3
Text: The pilot rank consists of three statuses: combat, trade and research. The battle rank can be raised by completing missions of hunting pirates and receiving a reward for the wanted pilots. Research rank is increased by completing tourist missions and selling research data. Trade rank is raised by completing trade missions and selling goods at the station. Subsequently, the rank will affect access to some closed systems.

Name: TutorialQuestT
Text:
Pay attention to the white exclamation marks on the galaxy map. They mean a side quest is available at one of the stations in the system. It can be found by visiting the bar at the space station. Have a drink and maybe someone will want to talk to you.

Yellow exclamation points on the system map indicate random events. According to the level of danger, you can estimate the risks of flying to this place. By visiting these events, you can get rare materials for upgrading ship modules and change the level of your karma.

Name: TutorialBattleT
Text:
Good efficiency in battle is the result of the correct choice of the ship and the configuration of its modules. It is worth choosing from combat and multipurpose ships. Combine energy cannons with kinetic cannons or missiles/torpedoes. Installing energy cannons alone will quickly deplete the capacitor charge and you will fire intermittently.

Also, do not neglect the protection of the ship. Upgrade your ship's shield, install hull reinforcements, shield cell banks (which quickly restore the shield).

It is strongly recommended to install defense turret module and chaff launcher module on all ships. All this significantly increase the survivability of your ship in battle, reducing the number of hits on it.

More powerful thrusters will significantly increase your ship's maneuverability, which can also turn the outcome of the battle in your favor. The faster your ship turns around, the more damage you will deal.

Don't forget to change the power priority. If you do not have enough power to fire continuously, change priority to cannons. If you are dealing with a more maneuverable enemy - set priority to the engines. You need to quickly restore the energy shield - set all priority to system modules and keep your distance with the enemy until the shield is restored.

There is nothing wrong with going into the warp to get away from the chase. At the same time, the preparation time for a warp jump can be increased. To survive this time, use protection systems (chaff launcher and defense turret), turn on the silent mode (acts similarly to chaff launcher, but heats up the ship).

Name: TutorialPowerT
Text: Some modules (cannons, engines and energy shield) consume a lot of power at peak demand. To ensure that there is enough energy for more than one volley of cannons, and that the shield is restored faster, there is such module as a power distributor. Distributor capacitors smooth out excessive power consumption and allow modules to work continuously for a long time. The charge in the capacitor (blue indicators) and the priority (white indicators) are displayed under the power priority toggle buttons. The higher the priority of a particular subsystem, the faster the charge of the corresponding capacitor is restored. If the charge in the capacitor is at zero, the cannons will stop firing, the shield will stop restoring. If the priority on the cannons does not give anything additional, except a faster recharge of the capacitor, then the other two systems are different. Priority on engines also increases the acceleration and maneuverability of the ship, and priority on systems increases shield strength.

Name: TutorialTradeT
Text:
Look for places where goods are cheaper, sell in places where this goods is more expensive. The filters on the galaxy map will help you with this. A green arrow indicates an excess of goods (the price will be below the average), and a red arrow indicates a shortage of the goods (the price will be above the average).

But at first, it will be more profitable not just to sell goods on the market, but to take tasks for transportation and search for goods.

Be careful when transporting cargo in systems with low security, avoid direct routes from the star to the station, as you may encounter pirates.

It is most profitable to trade illegal goods (slaves and tritonin). It can usually be bought on anarchy systems and sold on high security systems. But at the same time, it is necessary to avoid scanning the cargo by system guards, who may require you to drop the cargo and pay a fine. If, nevertheless, your ship is being scanned, then you can turn on the silent mode (in the external module's menu). This will abort the scan.

By upgrading your trading rank, you increase the reward for any trading tasks.

Name: TutorialBountyT
Text:
Pirate hunting is a profitable business, although it is quite dangerous. One way to cash in on this is to take on a mission at the station. After you arrive at the desired star system, inspect the map of the system. Perhaps the pirate's coordinates will be marked with a green exclamation mark. Sometimes the right pirate can be found next to the star.

The second option would be to install a criminal scanner module. Pirates are not wanted in all systems and often they are not marked as enemy (in red). To find out if there is a reward for a pilot in another system, you need to scan it with the criminal scanner module.

You can also help the guards in systems with security level "conflict zone". Dealing significant damage to a pirate will be richly rewarded.

Level up your battle rank and you will increase the reward for destroying pirates.

Name: TutorialExploreT
Text:
Exploring the depths of space will help you earn money by selling data at the station. By leveling up your researcher rank, you increase the value of your research data.

But, unfortunately, all star systems closest to the Sun have already been explored. Unknown stars and planets are 300 light-years away from the core systems. Such distances can be reached on a well-prepared ship. Ships from the "Explorer" and "Multipurpose" categories are best suited for flights over long distances. Such ships receive a significant increase in jump range due installing lighter ship modules.

Preparing a ship for long-distance travel should begin by installing all the main D-class modules (except for the warp drive, which is better to install an A-class). D-modules are the lightest, which means installing them will increase the jump range of your ship. In addition, you will need: a planetary scanner, a spectrometer, a fuelscoop, heat sinks, a repair module and a mining laser.

The planet scanner will allow you to detect unknown planets when you get close enough to them.

The spectrometer will allow you to display unknown planets on the system map and give you an information of the contents of these planets (indicates the direction to planets by the selected elements). The contents of the planets can indicate the presence of valuable/rare planets (for example, water and oxygen would probably indicate the presence of an Earth-like planet in the system).

The fuelscoop will give you the ability to refuel from the stars. Just be careful - not all stars can refuel the warp engine, which is indicated in the description of the system on the map of the galaxy.

Heatsinks can be useful if you overheat your ship during refueling or for other reasons.

The repair module can repair damaged modules. Parts for the repair module can be synthesized from ore, so it will not be superfluous to install at least one mining laser.

But why a repair module? How can a ship be damaged in deep space? Despite the almost complete lifelessness, space is quite dangerous. You may encounter space storms, black holes and neutron stars that can not only damage your ship, but even destroy it.

Besides, who knows what lives in the depths of space...

Name: TutorialMiningT
Text:
Mining and selling ore is a fairly profitable business. To do this, you will need to install the modules "Mining Laser" and "Spectrometer" on the ship. Ore is mined in asteroid belts. Such belts are indicated by shaded gray areas on the system map. Activate the spectrometer while in the asteroid belt to see the types of ore located there. To mine, activate your ship's guns by selecting mining lasers. Fly up to the asteroid at a close distance, turn the ship in asteroid direction and press the "Fire" button to start mining. The more modules like "mining laser" installed on your ship, the faster mining. After the ore breaks off from the asteroid, it will be displayed on the panel of nearby objects. By pressing the button of the nearest object, your ship will automatically collect ore.

The most profitable option would be to take tasks for the extraction of a certain ore. The place to sell a particular type of ore can be found through filters on the galaxy map. In systems with a shortage of ore (with a red down arrow icon), it will be possible not only to sell the mined ore, but also most likely to take on a task to mine this ore.

To speed up the process, you can also install a drone controller module that will automatically collect nearby resources.

Beware of pirates who hunt mining ships. Periodically change the area in which you mine ore. Try to avoid mining in unsafe systems.

Name: TutorialEngrnT
Text: Some stations have engineers. Engineers, with certain resources, can improve the modules of your ship. Engineers are marked with a gear symbol on the galaxy map (may be hidden behind side quest markers) and their presence is indicated in the system description. Each engineer proposes improvements to certain types of modules. Resources for installing improvements can be obtained on planets (when landing using a planetary vehicle), collecting parts from destroyed ships, visiting random events, destroying certain types of ships and using the energy trace scanner module. Collected materials are displayed in the cargo menu on the "materials" tab.

Name: TutorialRepT
Text:
Reputation should be increased separately at each station. Higher reputation gives access to more paid tasks. Reputation at each station is limited to 100 units. By successfully completing missions, selling research data, or earning bounties for slain pirates, you increase your station reputation.

Reputation at all stations is summed up in influence points. Influence points are needed to access some ship models and side quests that are related to certain factions.

Karma is an indicator of your integrity. Helping neutral ships [in trouble], destroying pirates (in events or for bounties), you improve your karma. If you transport of illegal goods, attack system guards or attack neutral ships, then you will reduce your karma. Too high karma will block access to quests in systems with anarchy and access to some side quests. On the contrary, too low a karma value will prevent you from accepting quests in high security systems and will also prevent you from accessing some side quests.

Name: TutorialFleetT
Text:
For your own protection or to deal with certain enemies, you can take mercenaries into your fleet. They can be found in the space station bar. But not every mercenary will agree to join your fleet. The higher your combat rank and the more expensive your ship, the more deadly pilots will be available for hire and the larger your fleet can be. You also need to know that their services are not free. They take a certain percentage of the money you earn.

Detailed information about your fleet and its management can be found in the fleet menu (opened through the onboard menu). You can set the behavior mode, the ability to kick out a mercenary, regroup and repair ships. In defensive mode, mercenaries will only attack ships that attack your ship or mercenary ships. Attack mode allows mercenaries to attack any target you choose. The regroup fleet button commands the mercenaries to return to you, which is useful when any of your ships are too busy chasing the enemy or they are fighting too far away from you.

The button for repairing mercenary ships will only work near the station. In addition to repair, pressing this button also resupply ammunition.
